pr_title: feat(network): remove Headers class and add headersArray method

issue_context.title: Header model semantic mismatch
comments:
Linking #7404 which is similar 
Looking at the code, and I am quite confused.

The headers get denormalized into two models - an array and a `Set`:

https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/blob/16b0a96e78ec3bbb0fbdb12ca1c14959ad42e7dc/src/server/network.ts#L326-L327

`headers()` appears to return the array version:

https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/blob/16b0a96e78ec3bbb0fbdb12ca1c14959ad42e7dc/src/server/network.ts#L398-L400

And the array version is *not* the lossy `[key: string]: string` model described in the manual:

https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/blob/16b0a96e78ec3bbb0fbdb12ca1c14959ad42e7dc/src/server/types.ts#L193

I also don't see the code anywhere that collapses repeated headers and joins them with line-breaks?

This code hasn't been touched in a year - how come this is so different from the the published version I got from npm?

If I could get the `{ name: string, value: string }[]` version of the headers, no problems, I could handle everything from there.

If the model is somehow lossy from the Chrome integration side or something, there's probably not much I can do from here...

(on a side note, the code that constructs the `Set` from the array is duplicated among several constructors and methods, and should be consolidated.)
Oh, I see... the release-branch is 200 commits behind master. 👀

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/103348/131520854-61d14557-7688-430b-8e37-b8672d9aec5f.png)

The release-branch has an entirely different header model:

https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/blob/cf1fd795a6efa00a1bbe0642e38bca2e1f65fe18/src/network.ts#L96

It also doesn't have the denormalization from the master branch, or the duplicate code.

What exactly is your process here? It looks like you're maintaining two different pieces of software. 😐
Yeah, we are well-aware of this problem. This goes back to the times when browsers did not allow us getting the raw header information. Certain network stacks (macOS, libsoup, libcurl) are harder to work with than Chromium's stack. We'll probably fix it at some point.

What is the exact problem you are resolving? Knowing the use case would help us prioritizing the fix.
@pavelfeldman I can see you're working on the master branch almost daily, so is that where you're planning the next major release? The release branch is (technically) for maintenance only, is that correct?

I'm just trying to understand the process and assess the status of this project, before committing myself to building a fairly large and complex project with it. 😄

> We'll probably fix it at some point.

I could probably help, but I'd need to know which branch is considered the "source of truth".

Are you releasing the master branch anywhere in public? I might want to try it out instead of the release branch.

> What is the exact problem you are resolving?

I needed to parse multiple `set-cookie` headers from the response - I found a way, by simply splitting the combined header values with `.split("\n")`, and that seems to work... But since this detail is unspecified, I'm afraid I'm relying on an implementation detail.

> This goes back to the times when browsers did not allow us getting the raw header information.

Yeah, what you're doing on the master branch seems less lossy and definitely more sensible - but also a bit problematic in terms of how it duplicates logic and denormalizes the header. If I'm going to commit myself to working with this in the long term, I'm mostly probing to see if/where I might be able to help, and this would be something I could easily jump in and fix.

But that only makes sense if there's an unstable/pre-release and I could actually use what I contribute... 🙂
The master branch is for the next release (1.15.0) and gets released daily under `npm install playwright@next`. The release-1.14 branch is for bugfix releases (patch releases) for 1.14.X when we need to backport changes.

Instead of modifying the current header functions we could add rawHeaders() to stay conform with semver.

> The master branch is for the next release (1.15.0)

Okay, that's great! I will give that a shot.

> Instead of modifying the current header functions we could add rawHeaders() to stay conform with semver.

Yeah, definitely - I'm not proposing a breaking change. The existing model works well for some use-cases, so. 🙂

Would you guys care to review a proposal PR, or do you prefer doing this work on your own?
Looks like this is landing with #8638

review_comments:
fetch API actually sends headers to server like below:

```
headers-a: value-a, value-a-1, value-a-2
headers-b: value-b
```

and headersArray() returns

```
[
  ['headers-a', 'value-a, value-a-1, value-a-2'],
  ['headers-b', 'value-b'],
]
```

Is it expected...?

I thought this test want to check the behavior with headers like

```
header-a: value-a
header-b: value-b
header-a: value-a-1
header-a: value-a-2
```

however it seems JS fetch API doesn't allow to send such request...
